summary: Set 114 S2 gave the step checklist its forward half. start_session now parses the session's numbered steps out of spec.md (via spec_admission.parse_step_texts - the same parser that enforces the session-size cap, so the size a spec is admitted at and the plan an operator is shown cannot disagree) and writes them into activity-log.json as pending entries carrying kind: plan-step. This does not reopen Set 111 S4's decision that the renderer never synthesizes plan rows; it is that decision's own remedy - the plan goes INTO the record, so the renderer keeps one rule. build_rows reconciles plan against reality: the plan owns each row's position, the logged step owns its content, an unplanned step appears (appended), a planned step nobody logged stays visibly [ ], and the here-marker prefers the unfinished logged step over an earlier pending planned row. Seeded once, never re-seeded, so a re-registration writes nothing and no mid-session write can stale a verification stamp. Four rounds. Round 1 (both discovery lenses independently) and round 2 found the same defect: the gate filters excluded only plan-step while path_aware_critique / contract_gate records - written at registration for any configured set - still counted as real work, so check_activity_log_entry could pass before any work existed. Fixed with one predicate, session_checklist.is_logged_step, used by _reconcile and both gates. Round 2 also found that an ordinal-first claim cascades when a spec is edited mid-flight: the inserted step claims one planned row, the shifted step claims the next, and the last planned row vanishes. The round-2 fix (identity before ordinal) was rejected by round 3, correctly - it only rescued the case where the shifted step's key matched a seeded slug. There is no signal inside the ledger (N logged steps, N planned rows, each number used once is the shape of both the intact and the renumbered case), so the fix looks outside it: plan_matches_spec compares the seeded step texts against spec.md now, and an edited, missing or unparseable spec withdraws ordinal matching entirely - unmatched steps append and no planned row can be evicted. No row ever comes from the spec. Round 4 VERIFIED with all four fixes accepted. 3765 pytest passed / 9 skipped; 33 Playwright passed (run because start_session is a state-file writer and now writes to activity-log.json, which the extension watches).

reason.specifics: Session 3 renders in the Work Explorer what Sessions 1 and 2 put in the record. The tree's children are build_rows' output; an orchestrator that does not know why a row can be is_planned, why ordinal reconciliation is gated on plan_matches_spec, or why the renderer is forbidden from inventing rows will either re-derive the plan in TypeScript - reopening a decision two sessions have now closed - or render a tree that disagrees with the checklist. It is also the set's terminal session (change-log.md, Step 9 review, advisory path-aware critique). Full reasoning and the four things S3 must not inherit uncritically are in ai-assignment.md.
